articles.title: The Strategic Case for AI During the Guest Visit — Not Just Before and After
articles.summary: Attractions.io argues that the industry is over-investing in pre- and post-visit AI tools while neglecting the high-value window when guests are actually on-site. With attendance flat but revenue growing, in-visit AI targeting secondary spend on food, retail, and premium experiences represents a significant untapped opportunity. FEC operators should evaluate how real-time AI tools could drive per-cap spending during the visit itself.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's technology chief outlines how AI and data integration are pushing ticketing and in-park purchasing far beyond simple transaction processing. The piece explores removing friction between guests and experiences as the central design goal for modern FEC tech stacks. Operators considering platform upgrades or new POS and ticketing systems will find this a useful strategic framing.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111 Editorial: Frictionless Guest Experience as the Industry's Core Design Goal
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's publisher frames the industry's defining challenge as eliminating every obstacle between the guest and the experience, from ticketing to in-park navigation. The issue covers AI, immersive Halloween activations, and competitive socializing, making it a strong read for operators planning 2027 investments. The frictionless experience theme is directly applicable to FEC layout, tech, and programming decisions.

articles.title: Ventola Projects Installs Immersive Ball-Responsive Bowling at Ecuador FEC
articles.summary: UK-based Ventola Projects has completed its first South American installation, delivering projection-mapped immersive bowling at PlayGo Entertainment in Mall del Alto, Cuenca, Ecuador. The system uses VAvR Alliance partner technology to create ball-responsive visuals across the lanes, elevating a standard bowling offering into a differentiated attraction. This signals continued global appetite for upgraded bowling experiences as a competitive socializing anchor in FEC environments.

articles.title: Premium Interactive Horror: How Six Flags and Warner Bros. Are Raising the Halloween Bar
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are investing in premium, interactive horror experiences tied to The Conjuring IP for the fall season. The piece examines how operators can command higher per-cap revenue during Halloween by offering tiered, immersive horror product alongside standard throughput events. FEC operators running seasonal scare events should study this premium-tier model as a revenue diversification strategy.

articles.title: Buying Immersive Attractions: Why Resolution Specs Can Mislead Operators
articles.summary: Simtec Systems warns that RFPs for dome theatres, flying theatres, and immersive spaces routinely specify resolution figures that have little correlation with actual guest experience, while ignoring brightness, contrast, and long-term image quality. The article offers practical guidance on what specifications actually matter when evaluating visual system purchases. Any FEC operator or supplier procuring large-format immersive tech should read this before issuing or responding to an RFP.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands Into Competitive Socializing with New Game-Based Concept
articles.summary: Experience design firm Jora Vision is broadening its portfolio into competitive socializing, a category showing strong growth across FEC and entertainment venue formats. The concept centers on skill-based gameplay designed for groups, aligning with demand for social, repeatable experiences that drive dwell time and return visits. FEC operators exploring competitive socializing additions will want to watch Jora Vision's rollout.

articles.title: Fun Spot America to Auction Atlanta Park Equipment on October 14
articles.summary: Fun Spot America has announced an equipment and asset auction for its permanently closed Atlanta-area park in Fayetteville, Georgia, scheduled for October 14, 2026. The park closed to guests on August 2, making this a significant opportunity for operators and suppliers looking to acquire amusement equipment at auction prices. FEC developers and ride buyers should monitor the auction listing for go-kart, arcade, and ride inventory.

articles.title: Texas' Largest Family Entertainment Center Set to Open in Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new FEC billing itself as Texas' biggest is set to open in the Houston market in 2026, signaling continued investor confidence in large-format indoor entertainment destinations. The development reflects the broader trend of supersized FECs anchoring mixed-use retail and entertainment districts. Competitors and suppliers in the Texas market should take note of the scale and amenity mix being planned.

articles.title: Malabar Group-Backed Playaza Entertainment Plans Six FEC Openings in 18 Months
articles.summary: Playaza Entertainment, backed by the Malabar Group, has announced plans to open six entertainment centres across India within the next 18 months, signaling aggressive expansion in one of the world's fastest-growing FEC markets. The rollout reflects rising middle-class demand for quality indoor leisure in Indian retail and mixed-use environments. Suppliers and equipment manufacturers looking to enter or scale in South Asia should take note of this pipeline.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer Growth but Rising Costs Pressure Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement and entertainment sector saw strong summer 2026 attendance growth, but operators are facing margin pressure from rising operational costs. The report highlights the tension between robust consumer demand and cost inflation that is familiar to FEC operators globally. Understanding India's trajectory is increasingly relevant as the market attracts international suppliers and franchise concepts.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Calls for GST Reduction to Boost Amusement Industry Growth
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries is lobbying for GST rationalisation, arguing that current tax rates suppress consumer demand and slow sector investment. This regulatory push has direct implications for FEC operators and investors targeting Indian market entry or expansion. A favorable GST outcome could significantly accelerate growth in one of the world's largest emerging FEC markets.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Drives UAE Attractions Boom
articles.summary: The UAE is experiencing a surge in indoor entertainment development, with major IP-anchored concepts and homegrown FEC formats expanding rapidly across the region. Rising temperatures and high mall foot traffic are structural tailwinds making indoor attractions particularly compelling for Gulf market investors. FEC operators and suppliers with international ambitions should assess the UAE pipeline closely.

articles.title: New Multi-Attraction Indoor FEC Planned for LaPorte, Indiana
articles.summary: A new indoor family entertainment center featuring bowling, mini-golf, arcade games, and additional attractions is in development for LaPorte, Indiana. The project reflects the continued expansion of multi-attraction FEC formats into mid-sized markets as developers seek to fill retail vacancies and serve underserved communities. Suppliers and operators can use this as a benchmark for typical amenity mix in new-build regional FECs.

articles.title: Ventola Projects to Launch Tetrapix EM4 Innovation at IAAPA Expo Europe
articles.summary: Ventola Projects will officially debut its latest VAvR technology, the Tetrapix EM4, at IAAPA Expo Europe in London this September. The company's immersive bowling and projection systems have been gaining traction globally, and this launch will be its highest-profile product reveal to date. FEC operators and attraction buyers attending IAAPA Europe should plan to visit Ventola's stand.

articles.title: IAAPA Expo Europe 2026 Preview: Key Themes, Exhibitors, and Innovations in London
articles.summary: IAAPA Expo Europe returns to ExCeL London from September 21–25, 2026, covering ride systems, immersive experiences, operations, sustainability, and guest engagement. The UK market is forecast to see 9.8% annual visitor spending growth through 2027, above the European average, making this a strategically important gathering for operators and suppliers. FEC professionals planning European expansion or sourcing new tech should prioritize attendance.

articles.title: Alterface Celebrates 25 Years of Interactive Attraction Design
articles.summary: Alterface, a leading developer of interactive shooting and experience attractions, marks its 25th anniversary with a retrospective on its role shaping interactive entertainment across themed and FEC environments globally. The company's systems are widely deployed in dark rides, interactive galleries, and FEC attraction formats. Operators evaluating interactive attraction investments can use this piece to understand Alterface's product philosophy and roadmap.

articles.title: Sportainment: How Sport Is Becoming a Full Entertainment Ecosystem
articles.summary: The blooloop analysis examines how live sport venues are evolving into multi-layered entertainment destinations combining dining, immersive installations, and premium hospitality alongside the core event. The sportainment model shares significant DNA with FEC competitive socializing formats and offers operators a framework for thinking about premium tiering and secondary spend. FEC developers building around sports simulation or viewing concepts will find this strategically useful.

articles.title: Lake Compounce Launches Phantom Fall Fest with New Family-Friendly and Scare Entertainment
articles.summary: Lake Compounce in Bristol, Connecticut, is running Phantom Fall Fest across 18 nights starting September 19, adding new family programming, food offerings, and elevated after-dark scare experiences. The dual-mode day-family and night-scare event structure is a model many FEC operators are adopting to maximize fall season revenue across different audience segments. Operators planning Halloween programming can benchmark against this well-established regional event.

articles.title: Adventureland Debuts New Haunted Experience for Phantom Fall Fest's Fifth Season
articles.summary: Adventureland in Altoona, Iowa, introduces MALICE: Jabberwocky's Revenge as the anchor new experience for its fifth annual Phantom Fall Fest, running from September 26. The park continues to invest in original IP-based haunted experiences rather than licensed content, offering a differentiated Halloween product. FEC and amusement park operators can take notes on building proprietary scare IP as a long-term brand asset.

articles.title: Heatwave Reduces Indoor Footfall at Hollywood Bowl, Deutsche Bank Cuts Target
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has trimmed its price target for Hollywood Bowl Group after a summer heatwave led to lower-than-expected indoor footfall at the UK bowling operator's venues. The note highlights weather sensitivity as an underappreciated risk factor for indoor FEC operators, even those in climate-controlled venues. Investors and operators with multi-site indoor entertainment portfolios should factor weather pattern variability into their revenue forecasting models.

articles.title: First Look: Renderings Released for MADCAPS Entertainment Center in Maricopa, Arizona
articles.summary: New renderings have been released for the planned MADCAPS entertainment center in Maricopa, Arizona, giving the industry a first visual look at the facility's design and attractions mix. The project adds to a growing pipeline of new FEC developments in the greater Phoenix market. Operators and designers can use the renderings to gauge current design trends in mid-size Sun Belt FEC developments.

articles.title: Launch Family Entertainment Brings Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola Market
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is moving forward with a new fun center on Davis Highway in Pensacola, Florida, combining arcade gaming and a trampoline park in a growing suburban market. The opening adds to Launch's expanding footprint and reflects sustained operator confidence in the trampoline-plus-arcade FEC format. Local competitors and suppliers in the Florida Panhandle region should monitor the opening timeline.

articles.title: SafeStrap Device Allows Roller Coaster Rides for Guests with Leg Prostheses
articles.summary: Efteling, in partnership with TU Delft and De Hoogstraat Rehabilitation, has launched SafeStrap, a safety strap that keeps leg prostheses securely in place during roller coaster rides without requiring removal. The innovation directly expands ride accessibility for guests with limb differences, a meaningful step for inclusive attraction design. FEC and amusement park operators focused on accessibility should evaluate whether similar adaptations are applicable to their ride portfolios.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, prompting community reaction and raising questions about the sustainability of legacy FEC formats in competitive urban markets. The closure is a reminder that even established multi-attraction venues face real lifecycle challenges as newer, more experience-focused competitors enter the market. Operators and investors should study the factors behind this closure as a cautionary case study.

articles.title: WildBrain CPLG to Develop Location-Based Entertainment for Miraculous IP Across EMEA and APAC
articles.summary: WildBrain CPLG has been appointed to develop location-based entertainment opportunities for the Miraculous animated franchise across EMEA and APAC markets. The deal signals growing appetite from IP holders to expand into FEC and attraction formats beyond traditional licensing categories. FEC operators seeking branded IP partnerships for kids' entertainment zones should watch this rollout for potential licensing opportunities.

articles.title: Attraktion! Installs Full Product Catalogue at Polish Adventure Park
articles.summary: Attraktion! has completed an installation of its full product range at a Polish adventure park, showcasing the breadth of its FEC-focused attractions portfolio in a single venue. The project serves as a live showcase for operators evaluating Attraktion! products for new builds or retrofits. European FEC operators and buyers attending IAAPA Expo Europe may want to use this as a reference site visit.

articles.title: Play Town Indoor Amusement Proposed for Milford, Connecticut
articles.summary: A new indoor amusement concept called Play Town has been proposed for a site in Milford, Connecticut, adding to a wave of FEC development proposals across the Northeast US. The project is still in the planning stage but reflects continued developer interest in converting underutilized retail space into indoor entertainment destinations. FEC industry stakeholders can track this as a representative example of the conversion-to-entertainment trend.

articles.title: Ten Years of PROJEKTIL: Lessons from a Studio That Turns Heritage Spaces Into Ticketed Attractions
articles.summary: Immersive entertainment studio PROJEKTIL reflects on a decade of staging ticketed productions in churches, museums, and heritage spaces across more than 100 cities globally. The piece covers the balance between creative ambition and commercial scalability, offering insights relevant to FEC operators developing immersive or pop-up experience formats. Operators exploring temporary or touring immersive attractions will find the business model discussion particularly useful.
